question_text: Mention the frequency range of speech signals.

Physics hand-checked: the standard telephone-quality speech band is 300 Hz to 3100 Hz, so the bandwidth is 3100 − 300 = 2800 Hz — the numbers and the subtraction both agree with the book.

recall_prompt: Say the frequency range used for speech signals and the bandwidth that range gives.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The range: 300 Hz to 3100 Hz
lines: For speech signals, the frequency range
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both end values, with the unit Hz on each.
steps.why: This is the band a telephone channel is built to carry: it is wide enough for speech to stay clear, and keeping it narrow lets many calls share one channel.
common_mistakes: Writing 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz. That is the range of human HEARING; the speech-signal band used in communication is 300 Hz to 3100 Hz.
Dropping the unit. Both limits need Hz.

recall.must_convey: That speech signals use the frequency range 300 Hz to 3100 Hz.

steps.memory_tip: Both limits end the same way: 300 and 3100 — a 3 at the front of each.

steps.label: The bandwidth: 2800 Hz
lines: The bandwidth is the difference between
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show the subtraction, not just the answer 2800 Hz.
steps.why: Bandwidth is defined as highest frequency minus lowest, so writing the subtraction shows the definition is known and makes the 2800 Hz impossible to get wrong.
common_mistakes: Adding instead of subtracting. Bandwidth is 3100 − 300, not 3100 + 300.
Writing 2800 without Hz. Bandwidth is a frequency and carries the unit.

recall.must_convey: That the bandwidth is the highest frequency minus the lowest, 3100 − 300 = 2800 Hz.

steps.memory_tip: Bandwidth is a width: top of the band minus bottom of the band.

insider_note: One mark per number pair: the range 300–3100 Hz, then the subtraction that gives 2800 Hz. The subtraction line is what separates this from a memorised figure.
